proposals.rationale: I made one edit to `plugins/core/skills/crew/references/conclave.md`. In the gap round's list of checklist kinds, `screen` was the only kind with no description beside it, so I added one: `screen` (a page, a dialog, a form, a view, or a component a view renders). The first four items come from the screen checklist's own description. Only one of the two `screen-checklist` failures is a real one. The engine prints `.packs/laravel/checklists/screen.md` only when `crew pack files checklists screen` runs, and earlier runs on this bundle that did run it passed. So the failing run most likely filed the alert component under another kind or `none`, and the gloss makes a Blade component on `welcome.blade.php` clearly a screen. I haven't seen the failing trace and haven't re-run the case. Another possibility is that the run took the fast route, which never reaches the gap round. The description can't fix that, and I didn't change the route rules. The two `honest-ending` failures are not about the harness: the judge's call hit the Fable usage limit, so there was no verdict on the ending. Re-running both cases once there's quota will score them. No test pins the edited sentence.

proposals.refusal: the probe set (10 cases, about 44.04 USD by the baseline's costs) is above what is left under the ceiling (14.11 USD); not probed
proposals.rationale: I made one small edit to `plugins/core/skills/crew/references/conclave.md`, in the "Pick the checklists" paragraph. The `screen` kind there now has a short definition: anything a person sees, such as a page, a view, a template, a component or a partial, in whatever the stack calls it (Blade, Vue or JSX alike). This was the only real failure. The `honest-ending` graders in both cases never scored the ending: they "threw" because the judge model hit its usage limit. So they're infrastructure noise, not a harness problem, and I didn't touch anything for them. The `screen-checklist` grader passes only when `crew pack files checklists screen` prints `.packs/laravel/checklists/screen.md` into the trace. A feature never takes the fast route, and the engine won't let a standard item into Plan without a checklist read. That means the failing run (one of three, going by the 0.14 spread) must have read a different kind, or recorded `none` with a reason. My guess is that it didn't see "an anonymous Blade component" as a `screen`, because `screen` was the only kind on that line with no definition next to it. I couldn't see the failing trace, so this cause is inferred and nothing has been re-run. The pinned strings on the page (the kinds line's `motion`/`design-contract`, the `crew pack files checklists` wording) are untouched. The new words don't include the pack's path, so `no-screen-checklist` in the absent case still holds.
